articles.title: ‘They looked like two curtain-twitchers, though not very subtle ones’: Peter Crome’s best phone picture
articles.summary: The photographer was walking home in London when he caught the attention of a pair of canine snoops. Walking home after dropping his little girl at school, Peter Crome sensed he was being watched.
body: The cause of his disquiet that day was, to his happy surprise, these two dogs. “It was such a comical moment,” he says. “They looked like two curtain-twitchers, though not very subtle ones. I liked how they were perfectly framed with the different layers of window frames, and the brickwork and hedge provided some pleasing textures, but it was the disapproving expression on their faces that made the photo for me.”

Crome waited for a while as the dogs watched other passersby, turning their heads in unison. He crossed the road to draw their attention, then took a single photo on his iPhone 14 Pro. “This is the sort of picture I would have sent my mum before she passed away a couple of years ago. I think this one would have really tickled her,” Crome says.

articles.title: Stacey Dooley: ‘My skirt fell down on the Strictly Live tour. I was wearing big borrowed stage briefs‘
articles.summary: The broadcaster on her days as a shoplifter, catastrophising, and a first kiss with her dance partner. Born in Luton, Bedfordshire, Stacey Dooley, 39, left school at 15 and worked as a shop assistant. In 2007 she was selected to take part in the BBC reality series Blood, Sweat and T-Shirts.
body: What is the trait you most deplore in yourself? I’m quite greedy. I achieve something or something’s feeling really brilliant and I’m, like, “Right, what are we doing next? What are we getting next?”

What was your most embarrassing moment? When I was doing the Strictly Live tour at the O2, my skirt fell down. So I am stood in the middle of the O2 in my knickers – and they weren’t even my knickers, they were big borrowed stage briefs.
What would your superpower be? To be able to hear what people say when we’ve left the room.
What makes you unhappy? I’ve become a lot more anxious since becoming a mum. Catastrophising about things is pretty grim.

In 2007 she was selected to take part in the BBC reality series Blood, Sweat and T-Shirts.

articles.title: Spa bliss in the Alps: hot springs and hiking in the shadow of Mont Blanc
articles.summary: An autumn break in the French mountain town of Saint-Gervais-Les-Bains offers thermal treatments and glorious walking trails before the winter ski crowds descend. Mont Blanc is hiding behind the clouds, but the Aiguille du Midi spears the sky above a mountainside ablaze with russet, gold and tawny…
body: Our little group has trundled up to Mont Lachat station (altitude: 2,115 metres) on the Tramway du Mont Blanc, the century-old cog railway that climbs improbably steep slopes from the French alpine town of Saint-Gervais-les-Bains. Operational since 1909, the railway was once intended to reach the 4,809-metre summit of Mont Blanc, but war, glacial terrain and waning funds put an end to that ambition. But even from Mont Lachat, the view is a showstopper. On one side, the Bionnassay Glacier slips scenically down the slope, a buzzard soaring over the milky-green glacial lake at its base, while on the other the Chamonix valley basks in soft autumnal sunshine.

Autumn is golden season in the Alps, when you can find quieter hiking trails, lower prices and air crisp enough to stir the senses without nipping your fingers. Once focused purely on winter sports, the region’s resorts have spent years building up their summer credentials to offer hiking and biking through flower-strewn meadows. Now they’re marketing their shoulder season, too, to meet a growing demand for off-peak escapes.

articles.title: Tim Dowling: at last I join the ranks of competent people
articles.summary: It’s not often I get the chance to admire my handiwork, but I have finally fixed a light switch. For a single strange moment, everything appears to be in hand: the garden is tidy and free of dead branches, thanks to Gardening Steve; the back door, which refused to close properly for most of the…
body: The bathtub’s clawed feet are sitting on two long planks, safely spreading its enormous load evenly across the squishy, sinking bathroom floor. There are, theoretically, further repairs to be undertaken here, but I’ve reached an age where I’ve had to make sharp adjustments to my idea of what constitutes a permanent solution. If nothing else happens, this will do.

The kitchen table has been sanded down and refinished, by me. At first the effect was a bit too orangey for my wife’s liking, but over the subsequent days the colour of the wood seemed to improve when contrasted with the prospect of doing the whole thing all over again.
As the nights draw in, only one real job remains: the kitchen’s three-button dimmer switch wall plate is broken – one of the main lights simply won’t come on.
“If you can find a like-for-like replacement for the switch plate, I can put it in,” I say, still more rashly.

articles.title: 7 Fall Decor Trends Worth the Investment, According to Interior Designers
articles.summary: As temperatures continue to drop, transform your space by shopping our favorite fall home decor essentials—here, interior designers share the trends to know.
body: As leaves turn russet and we retrieve our rollneck sweaters and leather boots from the depths of our closets, our interiors deserve a little refresh, too. (What season is better for nesting?) Any designer will tell you that the change needn’t be drastic; something as simple as upgrading your bed linens or introducing a new lamp can make all the difference.

Perhaps now is the time to invest in that piece of furniture you’ve had your eye on, or finally pull together a room that doesn’t quite feel finished with the help of an accent rug. Whatever you’re after, we spoke to 10 interior designers to discover the key fall home decor trends worth buying into this season.

You might assume that fall calls for a color palette of soft browns, reds, oranges, and yellows–but this year, it’s all about the richness of jewel tones and using certain shades with intensity. Take Sophie Rowell, founder of Côte de Folk, who, in one project, recently enveloped walls and floors in a deep olive green, adding a sense of tactility by forgoing hard flooring and rugs in favor of wall-to-wall carpet.

articles.title: Toasted Meringue Hazelnut Blondies
articles.summary: This isn’t competing with a brownie. It’s in a class of its own.
body: Place a rack in middle of oven; preheat to 325°. Lightly coat a 9x9" pan with nonstick vegetable oil spray. Line pan with parchment paper, leaving overhang on two sides. Toast 2 cups blanched hazelnuts on a rimmed baking sheet, tossing halfway through, until golden brown and fragrant, 15–18 minutes. Let sit until cool enough to handle, then coarsely chop; set aside.
Cook 1 cup (2 sticks) unsalted butter in a small saucepan over medium heat, stirring often, until butter foams, then browns (do not burn), 7–9 minutes. Remove from heat.

Whisk 2 large eggs, room temperature, 1 large egg yolk, room temperature, 1¼ cups (250 g) granulated sugar, ¼ cup (packed; 50 g) light brown sugar, 2 tsp. vanilla bean paste or vanilla extract, 1½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and ¾ tsp. instant espresso powder (if using) in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the whisk attachment on medium-high speed until mixture is pale and doubled in volume, 6–9 minutes (mixture will form an unbroken ribbon when whisk is lifted from bowl).

articles.title: The Ugly but Good Cookie I Walked 40,000 Steps For
articles.summary: In a world of viral pastries, what happens to introverted baked goods?
body: When you have to wake up before sunrise for your job, you fiercely guard the days you don’t. Which is why I was profoundly pissed when my alarm rang at 4:30 a.m. on a morning I was ostensibly off the clock.

The plan was to walk to Jersey City with Brooks Headley. (Okay, mostly walk, with a short ferry interlude, given the Holland Tunnel isn’t pedestrian-friendly.) Brooks, a pastry chef through and through, had suggested Bread and Salt, a bakery I’d never been to but had admired for years. We were going to meet in the East Village at 7:15 a.m. to start the odyssey. Because I like making things hard for myself, I decided to get there on foot. I had just signed up to write a column about long walks to food destinations—I needed to earn it.

For an urban trek, the outfit is imperative, so I fumbled in the dark for hiking shorts and a tank—a blessing for the scorcher ahead—anointed myself in sunscreen and tightened my Salomons. My route said two hours and seven minutes of walking, but the maps app and I are in a long-term acrimonious relationship wherein she underestimates my speed, and I beat her. I deducted 17 minutes from the estimate and set off.

articles.title: Carnegie Hall’s Opening Night Gala Spotlighted the Power of Music
articles.summary: When the first orange-tinged leaves appear in Central Park, New Yorkers knows the Carnegie Hall fall season is just around the corner, too. On Thursday evening, the historic venue opened its doors to mark the start of its autumn program with a performance by the Berliner Philharmoniker.
body: Led by chief conductor Kirill Petrenko and featuring star tenor Jonas Kaufmann, the night’s show under the Hall’s gilded ceilings and boxes was an international display of talent. In the heart of midtown Manhattan, the German orchestra performed a program of Italian music spanning Verdi, Leoncavallo, and Respighi, among others. A raucous standing ovation—and surprise brass musicians emerging from the wings—proved no translator was needed to manage the combination of different cultures at play, as they were all united by the rousing emotion of the opera.

“It was beautiful,” Constance Wu, a longtime classical music enthusiast, told Vogue. “It was a very pastoral, woodland-type of program, which is a wonderful thing to listen to as summer turns to fall. It was a cool, dusky vibe, and the sound was incredible.”

After the performance, the celebrations continued at Cipriani 42nd Street for the event’s annual gala. With a celestial ‘Where the Stars Align’ theme, guests including designer Prabal Gurung, Peter Sarsgaard, Doris Wong, Jessica Joffe, Lena Hall, and Eletra Wiedemann were surrounded by vibrant sunflowers and flickering candlelight under the venue’s soaring columns.
points: When the first orange-tinged leaves appear in Central Park, New Yorkers knows the Carnegie Hall fall season is just around the corner, too.

articles.title: How Milan Became Home to Europe's Best Cocktail Bar
articles.summary: One Milanese cocktail spot was just named the second-best bar in the world—but Milan has a long history as one of Europe's best drinking cities.
body: The World's 50 Best Bars for 2026 have just been revealed, and Milan has plenty to celebrate. Not only did Moebius Milano take second place in the global ranking, but it was also crowned the best bar in Europe. And, if that weren't enough, the awards ceremony itself took place in Milan on Wednesday, October 7, marking the first time the event has been hosted in Italy.

For a city that has always taken its aperitivo seriously, it's quite an achievement. Milan might be better known internationally for its fashion houses and design scene, but anyone who has spent an evening wandering around its neighborhoods will know that going out for a drink is practically part of a local's daily routine. And while the tradition of meeting friends for a pre-dinner spritz or negroni is hardly new, Milan's cocktail scene has evolved considerably in recent years, with a growing number of bars pushing the boundaries of what a night out in the city can look like.
points: One Milanese cocktail spot was just named the second-best bar in the world—but Milan has a long history as one of Europe's best drinking cities.

articles.title: At The Albies, Amal and George Clooney Make Sure the Real-Life Heroes Take Center Stage
articles.summary: As one would imagine, Amal and George Clooney certainly have no issue pulling a crowd. As such, the host table placement at their fifth annual foundation gala, The Albies, did not disappoint.
body: On George’s left sat his longtime co-stars and friends Laura Dern and Brad Pitt. On the actor’s right, rapper and activist Vic Mensa and Downton Abbey’s Lord Grantham himself, Hugh Bonneville. With the inimitable couple separated only by the table’s elaborate edible display of Italian delicacies, Amal, draped in a gilded off-the-shoulder sequin gown by Gucci, was shoulder-to-shoulder with Vogue’s Anna Wintour, musician Jackson Browne, and actress Emma Thompson.

Still, even in a room bursting with headline-worthy names, the Clooneys ensured the spotlight shone brightest on the evening’s honorees: Kyrgyz journalists Bolot Temirov and Makhabat Tazhibek Kyzy, Malawian girls’ rights activist Vanessa Mwangala, American photojournalist Lynsey Addario, Congolese NGO Justice Plus, and Microsoft Vice Chair and President Brad Smith.

When it came to choosing this year’s award recipients, George remarked, “You have to look at things that are going on in the news. We’re looking for people that are shining a light on [an issue], can help put a protective shield over someone, or prevent them from being thrown in jail or killed.”
